evals.prompt:
Here is a recent session I had. Based on what you see in this conversation, please propose any subagent(s) that would be useful for future sessions like this one.

[SIMULATED SESSION HISTORY]
User: I need to document our decision to use SQLite for the mobile app's local storage.
Claude: [drafted an ADR with this structure:
# ADR-0001: Use SQLite for Local Storage
## Status
Draft
## Context
...
## Decision
...
## Consequences
...]
User: The status values should be 'Proposed', 'Accepted', 'Deprecated', or 'Superseded by ADR-XXXX' — not 'Draft'. Please fix that.
Claude: [corrected the status field]
User: Good. Now I need to document our decision to use LWW (Last Write Wins) for conflict resolution in sync.
Claude: [wrote second ADR, ADR-0002, with the corrected status format]
User: Now one more — document why we keep updated_at as a plaintext ISO8601 string instead of a Unix timestamp integer.
Claude: [wrote ADR-0003]
User: Perfect. ADRs are stored in docs/adr/ by the way, numbered sequentially.
[END SESSION HISTORY]
evals.expected_output: A proposed adr-writer agent file with correct status vocabulary (Proposed/Accepted/Deprecated/Superseded), storage path, and trigger description

assertions.text: Output contains a complete agent file with YAML frontmatter (name and description fields)
Agent file encodes all four correct status values: Proposed, Accepted, Deprecated, and Superseded
Agent file explicitly states NOT to use 'Draft' (or similar incorrect values)
Agent file specifies a storage path for ADR files
The description field includes specific conditions that should trigger this agent

evals.prompt:
Here's a recent coding session. Please propose subagent(s) that could be useful in future sessions like this one.

[SIMULATED SESSION HISTORY]
User: I'm getting a compile error in my project. The error is: error[E0308]: mismatched types expected SpaceError, found anyhow::Error
Claude: It looks like there's a type mismatch. Could you share the relevant code?
User: Oh right — this is a Rust project called space-mobile. We use a custom error type `SpaceError` defined in src/error.rs. We don't use anyhow anywhere, everything returns Result<T, SpaceError>.
Claude: [suggested fix, updated function signature]
User: Run cargo check to verify it compiles first, then cargo test.
Claude: [ran cargo check — new error in a different file with same issue]
User: Before you touch the connection logic, check .space/config.toml — the db_path and sync_endpoint are configured there and the code reads from it at runtime.
Claude: [read config, adjusted fix]
User: Also SpaceError has variants: NotFound, SyncFailed, DbError, and ParseError. Make sure you're using the right variant.
Claude: [fixed all usages, ran cargo check — passes]
User: Great. Now cargo test.
Claude: [ran tests — 2 failing, fixed them]
User: Don't forget to run cargo check again after test fixes — last time you introduced a regression.
Claude: [ran cargo check, clean]
[END SESSION HISTORY]
evals.expected_output: A proposed agent that encodes SpaceError type and variants, config.toml lookup, and the cargo check→test→check workflow

assertions.text: Output contains at least one complete agent file with YAML frontmatter (name and description fields)
Agent file(s) mention SpaceError as the custom error type and forbid using anyhow
Agent file(s) list the SpaceError variants: NotFound, SyncFailed, DbError, ParseError
Agent file(s) encode the cargo check → cargo test → cargo check again verification sequence
Agent file(s) mention .space/config.toml and its role in connection/db logic
